posts.title: National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Extension Act
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary: The bill would extend the authority of the National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Foundation to build a monument in Washington, DC that honors emergency medical services workers and their service. This reauthorization would remain in effect for seven years after the bill becomes law.
posts.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Natural Resources Committee · Rep. Richard Hudson (R-NC)
posts.whatsNext: President has 10 days (Sundays excepted): sign, veto, or it becomes law unsigned (pocket veto if adjournment prevents return)

posts.title: Stop Secret Spending Act of 2025
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary: The bill would require federal agencies to publicly report spending on "other transaction agreements" (a type of contract that currently operates with less transparency and fewer regulations than standard government contracts) to the USAspending.gov website, where federal spending is tracked. It would also require the Treasury Department to publish annual reports showing how much federal spending data remains unreported and why, and would direct inspector generals at certain agencies to assess their spending data quality for the next decade.
posts.meta: Oversight and Government Reform Committee · Rep. Barry Moore (R-AL)
posts.whatsNext: President has 10 days (Sundays excepted): sign, veto, or it becomes law unsigned (pocket veto if adjournment prevents return)

posts.title: To remove restrictions from a parcel of land in Paducah, Kentucky.
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary: The bill would direct the Department of the Interior to remove various deed restrictions from a parcel of land at a military reserve center in Paducah, Kentucky that was transferred to the city in 2012, freeing it from easements, reservations, and other conditions that currently limit its use.
posts.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Natural Resources Committee · Rep. James Comer (R-KY)
posts.whatsNext: President has 10 days (Sundays excepted): sign, veto, or it becomes law unsigned (pocket veto if adjournment prevents return)

posts.title: Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary: The bill would extend federal tax breaks for people who suffered losses in major disasters and wildfires. It would allow taxpayers to deduct personal casualty losses from disasters occurring through the end of 2026, and would let people exclude wildfire relief payments from their taxable income if the fires were declared federal disasters between 2015 and 2026, regardless of when they receive the payments.
posts.meta: Finance Committee, Ways and Means Committee · Rep. W. Steube (R-FL)
posts.whatsNext: President has 10 days (Sundays excepted): sign, veto, or it becomes law unsigned (pocket veto if adjournment prevents return)

posts.title: Water Resources Development Act of 2026
posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Transportation and Infrastructure, as amended, H. Rept. 119-795
posts.summary: The bill would authorize and modify various water resources infrastructure projects managed by the Army Corps of Engineers, including efforts to maintain ports and harbors, improve navigation, reduce flooding and storm damage, restore ecosystems, protect shorelines, address harmful algal blooms, rehabilitate dams, and support water supply projects. It would also direct the Corps to create a new office to speed up project delivery and establish streamlined environmental approval processes for minor harbor and river improvements.

posts.title: Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (237-169)
posts.summary: The bill would prevent colleges and universities that participate in federal student aid programs from boycotting Israel for commercial reasons unless there is a valid business justification. It would also require schools receiving federal funding for international education programs to certify annually that they allow students and faculty to participate in academic programs in Israel on equal terms with other countries, and that Israeli students and faculty can participate in their programs on the same basis as those from other nations.
posts.meta: Education and Workforce Committee · Rep. Virginia Foxx (R-NC)
posts.whatsNext: To the Senate (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary: The law funds federal agencies through December 11, 2026, at current spending levels while preventing a government shutdown, with exceptions that provide additional or flexible funding for programs like nutrition assistance, disaster relief, and wildfire suppression. It also extends expiring authorities for agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, housing, and trade programs, while temporarily blocking certain regulatory changes and freezing congressional pay adjustments.
posts.meta: Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Jason Smith (R-MO)

posts.label: ❌ Failed passage (212-206)
posts.summary: The joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would require the Supreme Court to consist of exactly nine justices—one Chief Justice and eight Associate Justices.
posts.meta: Judiciary Committee · Rep. Andy Biggs (R-AZ)

posts.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary: The bill would extend through the end of 2028 duty-free trade benefits that allow most exports from eligible sub-Saharan African countries to enter the U.S. market without tariffs, while also extending customs user fees through the end of 2031. It would also allow for refunds of duties paid on African imports that entered the country after September 30, 2025.

posts.title: Hershel ‘Woody' Williams National Medal of Honor Monument Location Act
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary: The bill would authorize the National Medal of Honor Museum Foundation to build a commemorative monument on the National Mall honoring Medal of Honor recipients for their acts of valor and sacrifice. The monument would be required to be located within the central area of the National Mall, between the Capitol and Lincoln Memorial.

posts.title: Protecting Domestic Mining Act of 2025
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (218-201)
posts.summary: The bill would streamline federal environmental reviews for mining infrastructure projects by making them permanently eligible for expedited approval under existing transportation law. It would also block a separate government rule that would have narrowed expedited reviews to only critical minerals mining, preserving broader eligibility for various types of mining projects.
posts.meta: Natural Resources Committee · Rep. Jefferson Shreve (R-IN)

posts.title: Fair Credit Reporting Reseller Accuracy Act
posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Financial Services, as amended, H. Rept. 119-789
posts.summary: The bill would require companies that resell credit information obtained from other sources to follow reasonable procedures ensuring the accuracy of that information before passing it along to others. It would protect resellers from liability under credit reporting laws if they accurately communicate information they received from the original credit reporting agencies.
posts.meta: Financial Services Committee · Rep. Michael Lawler (R-NY)

posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Financial Services, as amended, H. Rept. 119-790
posts.summary: The bill would regulate companies that offer earned wage access services—allowing workers to draw a portion of their paycheck before payday—by establishing consumer protections and oversight requirements for these financial services.
posts.meta: Financial Services Committee · Rep. Bryan Steil (R-WI)

posts.title: STOP Payments Fraud Act of 2026
posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Financial Services, as amended, H. Rept. 119-792
posts.summary: The bill would amend federal banking law to create exceptions allowing banks to hold funds longer when they suspect a check or wire transfer is fraudulent, rather than being required to make deposited funds available within standard timeframes. It aims to give financial institutions more flexibility to prevent fraud losses while protecting depositors from schemes involving fake or stolen payment instruments.
posts.meta: Financial Services Committee · Rep. Young Kim (R-CA)

posts.title: Protecting Investors’ Personally Identifiable Information Act
posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee

posts.summary: The bill would prevent the Securities and Exchange Commission from requiring securities exchanges and their members to provide personally identifiable information of market participants for the Consolidated Audit Trail, a system used by regulators to track trading activity.

posts.title: HEIRS Act of 2025
posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Financial Services, as amended, H. Rept. 119-793
posts.summary: The bill would direct the Department of Housing and Urban Development to provide grants to states that adopt the Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act—a law designed to protect people who inherit property without a will from being forced to sell—and to nonprofits and legal clinics that help these heirs navigate ownership documentation, estate settlement, and property retention. It aims to address a historical problem where inherited property without clear title can be sold against the heirs' wishes by covering costs like legal fees, title searches, and recording expenses.
posts.meta: Financial Services Committee · Rep. Nikema Williams (D-GA)

posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Financial Services, as amended, H. Rept. 119-788
posts.summary: The bill would expand what positive financial information can be reported to credit agencies, allowing reports on whether consumers pay their rent, utilities, and telecommunications bills on time. It would also protect consumers in payment plans with energy companies from being marked as delinquent, and it would require a government study on how this expanded reporting affects consumers' credit access and financial well-being.

posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Financial Services, as amended, H. Rept. 119-791
posts.summary: The bill would exempt certain small, representative-owned personal services businesses from being classified as brokers under securities law, reducing their regulatory burden. It aims to clarify the regulatory status of these entities so they can operate more flexibly while still maintaining appropriate oversight.

posts.title: Northeast Lobsterman Protection Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House (219-196)
posts.summary: The bill would extend the deadline for the federal government to issue new regulations protecting endangered North Atlantic right whales from fishing gear entanglement, pushing the deadline from 2028 to 2035. It aims to give the lobster and crab fishing industries more time to comply with requirements to use existing or new technologies that reduce the risk of whales becoming tangled in their equipment.

posts.title: NDO Fairness Act of 2025
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would make it harder for the government to obtain court orders that delay notifying people when their emails and online communications are being accessed during investigations. It would require courts to issue written findings justifying these delays, limit them to 90 days for most cases (up to one year for child exploitation investigations), and ensure the orders are narrowly tailored to what's necessary. The bill would also require the Department of Justice to publicly report annually on how often these orders are used and who they target.

posts.title: Kayleigh’s Law Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed House with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would require federal courts to automatically issue lifetime no-contact orders prohibiting defendants convicted of violent crimes or sex crimes from contacting their victims, unless the court specifically terminates or suspends the order. These orders would take effect at sentencing and remain in place for the defendant's lifetime, with no fees charged to victims.
